messages:
Sam: Heads-up: experimenting with a header-prefetch arbitrator that decides between eager header materialize vs passive on-demand.
Priya: Curious, what's the decision boundary? arrival rate? warmup queue length?
Sam: Basic idea: cost model uses recent RPS, estimated shard fetch latency, and memory budget. If expected savings > cost_of_materialize -> materialize headers.
Diego: Might be noisy. Suggest smoothing the RPS window and adding hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping when model traffic oscillates.
Zoe: Also consider bundle characteristics: if manifest indicates many tiny shards, materializing headers buys more routing efficiency. For huge shards, headers don't help as much.
Priya: Agreed. We should also bias toward materialize for models with low eviction churn (long tail of requests).
Sam: Prototype config snippet I pushed to the branch:
```
arbitrator:
  rps_window_ms: 60000
  materialize_threshold_cost_ratio: 1.25
  header_prefetch_budget_pct: 0.02
  smoothing_alpha: 0.2
```
Diego: Nice. How do we protect against header cache fill by a storm (many concurrent model loads)? Need backpressure to avoid OOM.
Zoe: Backpressure idea: global circuit-breaker that converts materialize decisions to streaming when header_cache_usage > soft_limit. Emit events for devs to tune.
Priya: And for eviction policy: prefer LRU of full payloads but MRU for headers tied to active routing. So headers stay sticky for hot-serving replicas, payloads are evicted sooner.
Sam: Good plan. What about integrity checks on the small headers? If headers are corrupted, routing could send wrong offsets. Need fast checksum verification.
Diego: Use a compact 32-bit rolling checksum in header and full SHA256 in manifest. Verify rolling checksum on load, then async verify SHA256 for the header blob. If mismatch -> mark header invalid and fallback to streaming.
Zoe: Ops question: what metrics do we need in Console? I propose: header_materialize_count, header_validation_failures, header_eviction_count, header_cache_hit_ratio, materialize_to_stream_fallbacks.
Priya: Add also header_pressure_trips and arbitrator_decisions (counts per reason). Useful for tuning threshold.
infra-bot: job-schedule: header-arbitrator-canary -> eng-ml-canary-3 at 2026-03-25T02:30Z :white_check_mark:
Sam: Also planning a microbenchmark: simulate 10k concurrent model activations with mixed shard sizes and measure 95th token latency and disk IO. Will share results.
Diego: When you run it, include scenario with mixed-format bundles (safetensors + quant sidecar). We need to ensure header schema is format-agnostic.
Zoe: If we standardize header fields (offset, length, checksum, flags), sidecars can populate them. Add header_version so we can evolve safely.
Priya: One last thing: document the ABI change in manifest schema and add compatibility shim in demux. Don't break older runtimes.
Sam: Yup. I'll open a follow-up RFC with prototype, benchmarks, and proposed manifest patch. Thanks all :rocket:
